questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

His first movement after the shock ________ to work in his loom; and he went on with this unremittingly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is a compound sentence and there are two verbs in this sentence named **'had been'(BE**) and **'went'.**
 
• "he **went **on with this unremittingly" in this part of the sentence we find '**went' **is the past indefinite form of verb **'Go**'. So the tense of the entire sentence is in past. 
 
• Two verbs with their past indefinite form **can not co-exist together **in a same sentence. Because two facts can not happen at the same time. For example-
 
 
• The patient **had died **before the doctor** came.**
 
• The school prayer **had started** before I** reached.**
 
 
 
• So while there are two main verbs present in a sentence in **past tense**, one of the verbs must be placed in its **past participle form (V3)** in order to justify its action earlier than the other verb present there.
 
• Two main verbs in this sentence are '**be'** and '**go'.** Since '**went' **is in past indefinite form , **'be'** verb should be placed in its** past participle** form . So the correct answer is '**had been'.​**

​Therefore, the correct statement is **His first movement after the shock had been to work in his loom; and he went on with this unremittingly. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The 1st option is **incorrect** as '**was been**' is the past indefinite form of verb '**be' **and it is in **passive voice.** That doesn't signify the meaning of the sentence.
 
• The 2nd option is** incorrect **as '**has being**' is an incorrect structure of tense. As** V3** is to be placed after **have/has/had,** but here being is a** V4 **form of '**be**' verb. Moreover '**has' **is present form so it doesn't go with another verb which is in** past** in the same sentence. 
 
• Option 4 is **incorrect** as **'have been'** is signifies** present** tense of the **action/verb**. So it can not be used having another verb in **past tense** in the same sentence.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I can't wait to __gone camping__ next weekend.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In this sentence** 'to' **is used as an infinitive,** not as a preposition.** So, infinitive **'to**' is generally followed by** V1 form of the main verb. **
 
• Here **'go**' is the **v1** form of the main verb and **'camping' **is the present participle form used here. 
 
• As this is a simple sentence and there is no conjunction in this sentence, we must keep only one verb in this sentence and that is** 'wait**' here. '**can't** ' is modal verb used here with the main verb **'wait'**. So **'to go' **is an infinitive ( V1 form after infinitive is not considered as verb ) and '**camping'** is a participle form. As **two v1 form of verb** can not be placed together after infinitive** 'to'.** So "**go camping'** will be the** correct answer.**
 
• **Format = subject + verb + infinitive+ V1 form of verb + participle + object**
 
• Some more examples are as follow
 
 
• Suresh wants to visit Mussoorie **to practice climbing** there.
 
• I can't wait to watch the movie released yesterday. ** **
 
 

 Hence, the correct answer is** I can't wait** **to go camping** **next weekend.**

questions.question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

Sapna was abstracted, biting her lip restlessly and reading over the guide-books to the battle-field that Suraj (had brought along).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is in past tense and it is a complex sentence, so there are two verbs and they both are in past tense. One of them** being past indefinite,** another must be in** past participle form.**
 
• 'Sapna **was abstracted' **. Here **'was abstracted'** is written in** passive voice **but it is **past indefinite **in tense.
 
• So the another verb '...that Suraj** had brought along'** is in **past participle form.** Here the format is in **active voice. **
 
• **Rest of three options are in present tense.** In a sentence we can't place** present and past tense **of verbs together if they indicate some actions happened **at almost similar time. **

 Hence, The correct sentence is** Sapna was abstracted, biting her lip restlessly and reading over the guide-books to the battle-field that Suraj (had brought along).**

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

We had been collected and studied over 14,000 dung beetles from 98 different species.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 'We had been collected and studied...' is passive voice in sense. But in this sentence the passive voice doesn't make any sense here. As the passive structure of past perfect tense given here is **Subject + had + been + past participle form of main verb (V3) + object**
 
• The correct format should be '** We had collected and studied over 14,000 dung beetles from 98 different species.' **We must **omit 'been' **from this sentence. The correct format for this will be **Subject + had + V3 + object **
 
• **​**Some more examples are as follow 
 
 
• They **had advertised **for the company over the past two years.
 
• My cousin** had left** our home before I** returned** to Goa.
 
 

​Hence, the correct sentence is '**We had collected and studied over 14,000 dung beetles from 98 different species'.**

• The word "grate" is a misspelling of **"great,"** which means of an extent, amount, or intensity considerably above the normal or average. (महान)

 
 
• **Example: **He did a great job on his presentation.
 
 
 
• "Agelity" is a misspelling of **"agility,"** which refers to the ability to move quickly and easily. (चुस्ती)
 
 
• **Example: **The gymnast's agility was impressive during the performance.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct words are **"great"** (महान) and **"agility"** (चुस्ती).

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

• **Example:** The cheese was grated over the pasta.
 
 
 
• **Agelity**: Incorrect spelling of "agility" (चुस्ती).
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The man walks with a great deal of poise, in fact, very much like an elephant, but he also has the agility of the panthur.
 
 
• **Panthur**: Incorrect spelling of "panther" (तेंदुआ).
 
 
• **Example:** The panther moved silently through the jungle.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The man walks with a great deel of poise, in fact, very much like an ephalnt, but he also has the agility of the panther.
 
 
• **Deel**: Incorrect spelling of "deal" (सौदा).
 
 
• **Example:** Let's make a deal.
 
 
 
• **Ephalnt**: Incorrect spelling of "elephant" (हाथी).
 
 
• **Example:** The elephant is the largest land animal.
